newsitem.title: INDIA: India HLL may enter ice-cream manufacture.
newsitem.headline: India HLL may enter ice-cream manufacture.

text.p: India's Hindustan Lever Ltd (HLL), a subsidiary of the Anglo-Dutch giant Unilever Plc is considering making ice cream, its officials said on Friday.

"We are considering new capacities for ice cream after the dereservation," HLL chairman K.B. Dadiseth told a news conference, referring to the removal of ice cream from the government list of industries reserved for small-scale industries.
Ice-cream was taken out of the list of industries reserved for small-scale industries in the 1997/98 (April-March) budget presented to parliament last month.
"Till now we were only in frozen desserts," A. Lahiri, director of human resources and corporate affairs said.
Dadiseth said the firm would build a cold storage chain.
He said test marketing in table salt and wheat flour were very encouraging. "We are now building the bottom of the food business from where we would grow," Dadiseth said.
Both Kissan Annapurna salt and wheat flour would be launched across the nation in 1997. Dadiseth said these products though not commanding high margins, had a low capital investment.
"The company will continue to invest strongly in the Kissan range to build a critical mass," a company statement said.
"We must give Indians what they eat," Dadiseth said.
Analysts said the merger of two Unilever firms - HLL and Brooke Bond Lipton India Ltd -- was partly aimed at giving a boost to Unilever's thrust in the Indian food business.
